description: Kansas WIC provides approved foods and nutrition support through local clinics. A new applicant can start with the state’s online pre-application.
introduction: Kansas WIC provides approved foods and nutrition support through local clinics. A new applicant can start with the state’s online pre-application.

sections.who: Kansas residents may qualify during pregnancy, breastfeeding through the baby’s first birthday, or non-breastfeeding postpartum through six months. Infants and children under five also qualify when income and nutrition-risk conditions are met.
sections.get: The WIC card buys approved foods. Clinics provide nutrition education, breastfeeding support and referrals.
sections.docs: Bring applicant and child identification, Kansas residence evidence and household income proof. Ask the clinic which records it accepts for your circumstances.
sections.apply:
1. Use the pre-application linked from Kansas WIC’s family page; a local agency contacts you for an appointment.

  2. Attend the clinic assessment. If transferring from another state, contact WIC directly instead of submitting the new-applicant pre-application.
sections.after: Follow clinic appointments and food-shopping instructions. If moving away, ask for a Verification of Certification to help transfer services.
sections.sources:
Application and program details: Eligibility and first appointment, WIC services and transfers.

faqs: Does the pre-application immediately approve benefits?
No. The local clinic arranges eligibility and nutrition screening.
Should an interstate transfer use the pre-application?
No. The state directs transferring participants to contact WIC instead.
Yes. Income and the other WIC conditions determine eligibility.
What should I request before moving?
Ask the clinic for Verification of Certification.
